title: Class Interface with Mixed Levels of Abstraction
pattern: A high-level business domain struct exposes low-level container, iteration, or collection-style primitive methods in its public API.
why_bad: It presents an inconsistent, hodgepodge interface that mixes high-level concepts with raw data-structure traversal mechanics. It breaks encapsulation by leaking the fact that the underlying implementation uses a linear list or vector.
detection: A struct whose public API contains both domain-specific methods (e.g., `add_employee`) and collection-generic methods (e.g., `next_item`, `first_item`, `get_index`).
counterexample: Custom iterator structs designed intentionally to implement the standard library `Iterator` trait as a separate, distinct type.
fix: Hide the container implementation entirely, and expose only high-level domain services or provide a dedicated, separate iterator type.
source: Steve McConnell, *Code Complete* (2004), Chapter 6, Section 6.2 ("C++ Example of a Class Interface with Mixed Levels of Abstraction").
